history.summary: The Bhawani Amba Temple is one of the oldest shrines in Ambala; its exact date and period of establishment are still not figured out, but local tradition holds it has stood for several centuries. Tradition holds that Ambala derives its name from Goddess Amba, the presiding deity - one of three competing origin stories (the others being the 14th-century Amba Rajput founder and 'Amb Wala', the mango-village), and there is no historical evidence confirming the derivation (per tourmet.com). The temple features old carved pillars and intrinsic wall carvings reflecting the artistry of a bygone era. NOTE on CSV parenthetical 'Sheetla Mata': primary sources describe this shrine as dedicated to Amba/Bhawani Devi; a separate Mata Sheetla Temple is listed in Ambala's Old Town (verify whether the parenthetical indicates an additional deity here or conflates two shrines). town_description: Ambala is a major city in Haryana on the Punjab border, split into the twin hubs of Ambala City and Ambala Cantonment. It is one of North India's most important railway junctions, has a large military cantonment and Air Force presence, and is famous across India for its cloth and scientific-instrument markets. Tradition links the city's name to Goddess Amba (Bhawani Amba), whose ancient temple stands in the city.
